title: Aligning token attribution for embeddings, reranker pipelines, and tool-invoked outputs (non-chat endpoints)
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: We have multiple inconsistencies in how token/embedding/compute usage is attributed and billed for non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank pipelines, and any code path that invokes external tools/function-calls and then emits structured output). This ticket consolidates the accounting model so that: (1) every token and compute unit consumed during a request pipeline gets a single authoritative attribution record; (2) quotas and rate limits apply consistently regardless of whether a call returns streaming tokens, structured output, or triggers an async tool invocation; and (3) we provide corrective retroactive reconciliation for detected past discrepancies.
description_more: Background: Recent customer reports and internal audits found three classes of problems: A) function-calls that run third-party tools (or internal microservices) sometimes return structured payloads that bypass our token accounting layer, causing underbilling and quota miscounts; B) reranker pipelines that fan-out to multiple model invocations occasionally double-count shared prefixes or shared KV-cache hits; C) embedding-only endpoints used in pipelines are not uniformly attributed to the originating route/project and can be billed to the model default instead of the calling customer in some routing fallback cases. These issues cause customer-visible anomalies (unexpected quota exhaustion, spikes in usage metrics) and risk revenue leakage.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Implement a standardized 'usage event' envelope emitted by the infra layer for all non-chat model calls. 2) Usage events must include: request_id, customer_id, route, model_variant, token_counts (request/response), embedding_units, compute_ms, and caller_phase (ingest|model|postprocess|tool-exec). 3) Rate limiter enforcements read from the unified usage events so quota checks happen pre- and post-tool-exec for synchronous flows; async tool invocations must reserve tokens upfront when specified by route policy. 4) Add e2e tests that simulate: reranker fan-out with shared KV cache, embedding reuse in pipelines, and tool-call structured outputs. 5) Dashboard shows per-route and per-model reconciled totals and a list of corrected historical adjustments. 6) No customer-visible output changes other than more accurate billing and quota behavior.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): instrument a proof-of-concept usage event in a staging reranker service; validate that a downstream billing worker can reconstruct costs. Phase 2 (core changes, 2 sprints): expand the envelope across embedding and function-call paths, add pre-reservation support for async tool-calls, and update rate limiter to consult unified usage stream. Phase 3 (QA + rollout): run synthetic traffic and compare reconciled totals against current accounting for a 7-day window; gradually roll out with canary and per-customer feature flag. Phase 4 (retroactive corrections): implement a reconciliation job that emits adjustment events for any >0.5% variance over the comparison window. Rollout notes: default to conservative reservation to avoid underbilling; expose a console toggle for aggressive/full reconciliation.
risks_and_tradeoffs: - Pre-reserving tokens for async tool-calls can increase apparent quota consumption and may surprise some customers; mitigation: configurable route policy and clear console messaging. - Adding a unified envelope imposes perf overhead in the hot path; mitigate by batching usage events and sampling detailed traces only for high-cost calls. - Retroactive billing adjustments are operationally sensitive; require billing/finance sign-off and an audit trail for every adjustment.
work_items: Schema: usage event definition and proto + migration plan
Implement: embedding endpoint hooks to emit envelope
Implement: tool-call reservation API and enforcement
Update: rate limiter to integrate post-exec counters
Dashboard: reconcile view and correction queue
Docs: public changelog and internal playbook
Billing: reconcile job and finance review
